subject: Prospect Q&A: where LLM requests are executed, subprocessors, and deletion SLA
messages:
From: Anna Cho <anna.cho@healthframe.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick Q: where do requests run + deletion process

Hi Soojin / Marcus,

We're putting together a short security packet for our procurement and security teams and need a concise explanation of two things: where Redwood executes inference for hosted customers (region-level detail and any common hops), and what the deletion/retention SLA looks like for transient request data and cached KV state.

Specifically:
- Can you list the cloud regions used for US-hosted requests and any third-party subprocessors that touch request payloads?
- Do requests ever route through other regions (e.g., fallback to Europe) under normal operations or only for disaster scenarios?
- Is the KV cache persisted to disk anywhere, and how quickly can we ensure all cached data is flushed/erased after a deletion request?

We're a prospect evaluating Redwood for an API-first UX that will process PHI-like annotations; procurement asked for clear evidence we can restrict processing to US-only and meet a 30-day deletion SLA for cached artifacts.

Can you point us to a short evidence pack or CSV listing subprocessors as well?

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Cho
Head of Security Operations, HealthFrame
anna.cho@healthframe.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Cho <anna.cho@healthframe.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-19T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q: where do requests run + deletion process

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list of asks. Quick answers up front, then a short technical note and links to the evidence pack.

Summary answers: 
- US-hosted requests: primary execution regions are us-west-2 (Oregon) and us-east-1 (N. Virginia). We also operate dedicated pools in us-west-1 for certain customers on Dedicated capacity.
- Subprocessors: we use a small set of cloud infra providers (AWS), managed database providers for logs/metrics, and a CDN for control-plane assets. The attached CSV lists subprocessors and contract roles.
- Cross-border routing: by default requests stay in the pinned region. Smart routing only forwards to a different region if that region is explicitly enabled for the tenant or if there is an availability fallback; cross-region fallback is opt-in for customers concerned about availability.
- KV cache: the inference KV cache is an in-memory, GPU-local structure for active sessions. We do not persist session KV cache to long-term disk for hosted API requests; transient spill to ephemeral NVMe is encrypted and erased on instance termination. Cache flush/erasure for a deletion request is typically immediate for active sessions; complete purge from ephemeral storage is completed within 24 hours and we can provide an erasure confirmation.

Evidence pack & attachments: I've attached a short "processing evidence" PDF and the subprocessors CSV. The PDF contains region maps, our routing policy excerpt, and the KV/cache lifecycle.

Technical clarifications (Marcus cc'd):
- For Hosted API customers we support region pinning at the account level. If you require US-only guarantees we can lock processing to the two US regions listed above and disable fallbacks to other regions.
- For Dedicated customers (reserved capacity) we provide guaranteed placement on the customer's pinned pool and supply SLA language as part of the contract.
- Deletion SLA: for request payloads stored in transient logs we have a 30-day retention by default; we also offer a 7-day retention profile for enterprise customers and can negotiate shorter windows on Dedicated/Private deployments. Deletion requests trigger immediate logical deletion, and physical purge from backups follows the timeline in our deletion policy (we document backup rotation times in the evidence pack).

I'll loop Marcus in for a short note on KMS/HSM and audit evidence. If you want, we can schedule a 20-minute call tomorrow to walk through the pack.

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Cho <anna.cho@healthframe.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-20T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q: where do requests run + deletion process

Hi Anna — adding a technical supplement on keys, backups, and export controls.

Keys & encryption:
- Customer data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.3) and at rest. For hosted accounts we use a customer-key option backed by AWS KMS; for Private/Dedicated we support customer-managed HSM integrations.
- Audit logs record key usage and region where the key was used; those logs are available via the Console with appropriate retention windows.

Backups & deletion mechanics:
- Nightly snapshots of control-plane metadata are retained for up to 30 days by default. Snapshots are region-tagged and encrypted; physical deletion of snapshot slices occurs during our scheduled retention purge and can take up to 72 hours from the logical deletion request to complete across all copies in a region.
- For customers requiring stricter guarantees we offer a contract addendum: a 7-day snapshot-retention profile and an accelerated purge of ephemeral artifacts on Dedicated deployments.

Cross-border transfer specifics:
- We do not replicate request payloads to other regions for analytics by default. Aggregated, anonymized metrics may be processed outside the pinned region unless explicitly disabled.
- Where subprocessors (for example, third-party support tooling or monitoring vendors) have global footprints, the subprocessor CSV indicates whether they process data globally or are restricted to specific regions. All subprocessors are subject to our DPA and Standard Contractual Clauses where applicable.

Operational evidence we can provide on request:
- Subprocessor contracts and roles, redacted as needed.
- KMS usage logs and region-scoped audit trails (sample).
- A one-page export control statement showing routing rules and fallback conditions.

Happy to jump on a call and walk through the snippets — can do 30 minutes tomorrow 10:00–11:00 PT if that works for you.

Cheers,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Thanks Soojin and Marcus — this is exactly what procurement and InfoSec needed. A couple quick follow-ups: 

1) Can you confirm in writing that if we request US-only processing and disable fallbacks, no telemetry, logs, or snapshots will be exported outside the US for our tenant?
2) For the KV cache: you mentioned spill to ephemeral NVMe. If we request immediate purge, is the 24-hour window a maximum or typical? Procurement wants a written commitment they can sign.

If you can reply in thread with short bullets for procurement to paste into the SOW, that would speed things up. Also, please upload the subprocessors CSV to the Hubspot company record (link below) so procurement can download it.

HubSpot company link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/9876543

Appreciate it — if you can send the two one-paragraph bullets and the HubSpot upload confirmation, I'll move this to procurement review.

Best,
Anna
